conditions: Native Alpine apk, nonroot UID/GID 3000:3000, read-only root/input mounts, no network. No ARM target execution or installation.
joins: Require separately bound original APK/public-key hashes and a single scoped public key, run native apk verify and then adbdump --format json on that same file, bind all native info fields to the actual installed header and original package receipt, reconstruct complete Path-ordered artifact inventory with safe symlink referents, bind every real installed payload path/permission/checksum to the signed ADB metadata. No APKv2 parsing is applied to APKv3.
checksum_distinctions: The reviewed owned APKv3 installed f:S records use legacy Q1 tokens containing SHA256-160 for regular bytes or symlink text. The installed package checksum is compared as an opaque native metadata token, not mislabeled as APKv2 compressed-control SHA1. Full signed file SHA256 and original native package/payload verification are independently enforced. The separate BusyBox APKv2 survey found SHA1 per-file/link tokens; its control SHA1/payload SHA256 rules must not be conflated with this package.

negative_controls.actual_payload_mutation: One embedded source-helper PAYLOAD byte changed in a separate copy; original signed metadata/signature blocks and native adbdump JSON stay exactly unchanged. Native apk verify with the original scoped public key rejects exit 1: file integrity error.
negative_controls.actual_installed_record_mutation: A validly encoded installed file checksum changes with original installed package C token, original signed APK and key unchanged. Full wrapper rejects owned installed payload checksum differs from signed ADB.
negative_controls.dangerous_mutant: Bypassing the installed-file checksum guard makes both recorded architecture regressions fail with DID NOT RAISE InputError.

regression_tests.layer: Native AMD64 Alpine component/source/workflow subset, including complete real AMD64/ARM64 ADB metadata/installed-record fixtures and mocked process-failure guards; actual native tool/payload checks are the separate receipts above

scope: Owned native original package signature/payload, metadata/artifact inventory and complete actual installed database correspondence only. Final live installed files and component source/compiler/attribution joins, the three BusyBox owned package consumer joins, full aggregate source/security and MCP acceptance remain unfinished. No RPM dispatch change, missing-origin blanket skip, runtime trust/repository change, package install or target/source program execution. Original failures and candidates retained.
